newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. puts forces on standby for Albania evacuation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. puts forces on standby for Albania evacuation.

text.p: The U.S. military said on Wednesday it had put a naval battle group on standby in the Adriatic Sea in case Washington decided to use troops to evacuate more than 2,000 Americans living in Albania.
"We are basically in a standby mode," a spokesman at the U.S. European Command in Stuttgart, which oversees American military operations in Europe, told Reuters.
"We have pre-positioned equipment and a contingent of marines should there be a need for a mission. But there are no orders to execute," he said.
The battle group is clustered around the helicopter carrier USS Nassau and has about 2,000 marines attached to it, the spokesman said.

Prospects for a military mission grew on Thursday after international airline officials reported that Tirana airport was closed, hampering the evacuation of some foreign embassy staff and families ordered by their governments.
The U.S. State Department on Wednesday ordered 160 government employees and their dependants to leave by regular or charter flights. Another 2,000 Americans were urged to go.
The military spokesman said the ships in the battle group Nassau would remain near the Albanian coast in case any order for an evacuation came from the U.S. government.

Albania, the poorest of the Balkan countries, has been hit by an insurrection that started with protests by tens of thousands of people who lost their savings in high-risk investment funds that collapsed.
